content: Children diagnosed with type 1 diabetes are at an increased risk of developing other autoimmune conditions, including thyroid dysfunction. It is recommended to test for thyroid antibodies, specifically antithyroid peroxidase and antithyroglobulin antibodies, at the time of diabetes diagnosis and periodically thereafter if the results are positive. Monitoring thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels at the time of diagnosis or shortly after is particularly important, especially if maintaining stable glucose levels proves to be challenging. If the initial TSH levels are normal, it is advised to recheck TSH every 1 to 2 years, or sooner if the child exhibits symptoms of thyroid dysfunction or has a positive family history of thyroid-related conditions. Thyroid dysfunction, such as hypothyroidism, can have significant effects on growth and metabolic control, necessitating careful monitoring and management in children with type 1 diabetes.
